     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	Google Cloud Blog — "1,001 real-world gen AI use cases from the world's leading organizations"  
     6	URL: https://cloud.google.com/transform/101-real-world-generative-ai-use-cases-from-industry-leaders  
     7	Published: April 12, 2024; last updated: October 9, 2025

     9	
    10	![1,001 AI use cases from Google Cloud customers](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    11	
    12	## Overview and Growth Trajectory
    13	
    14	Google Cloud first published its list of real-world generative AI use cases during Cloud Next 24 in April 2024, starting with 101 entries. By October 2025, the list had grown **10×** to 1,001 use cases — and the authors note this still only scratches the surface of what is becoming possible.
    15	
    16	The list is organized by **11 major industry groups** and within those, **6 agent types**: Customer, Employee, Creative, Code, Data, and Security. The October 2025 edition added 400 new entries (denoted with an asterisk). Organizations span top companies, governments, researchers, and startups worldwide.

    18	The 11 industry verticals are:
    19	- Automotive & Logistics
    20	- Business & Professional Services

    32	
    33	![Automotive & Logistics](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    34	
    35	The Automotive & Logistics vertical provides one of the richest cross-sections of agent types. Below is a representative sample:

    38	|---|---|---|---|
    39	| Customer | Mercedes-Benz | MBUX Virtual Assistant powered by Gemini via Vertex AI enables natural driver conversations for navigation and POI | Natural language in-car assistant |

    43	| Customer | UPS Capital | DeliveryDefense Address Confidence uses ML to score delivery success likelihood | Data-driven delivery confidence |
    44	| Customer | PODS / Tombras | "World's Smartest Billboard" on trucks adapted to NYC neighborhoods in real time using Gemini | **6,000+ unique headlines**, 299 neighborhoods, 29 hours |
    45	| Employee | Toyota | AI platform on Google Cloud enables factory workers to build and deploy ML models | **10,000+ man-hours/year** saved |
    46	| Employee | Uber | AI agents summarize CS communications and surface prior interaction context | Improved CS rep effectiveness |
    47	| Employee | Rivian | Gemini in Google Workspace for instant research, accelerated learning, and rapid skill acquisition | Faster onboarding and deep research |
    48	| Employee | Rivian | NotebookLM centralizes FAQ answers with verified sources and interactive chat | Reduced repetitive inquiries |
    49	| Employee | Geotab | Google Workspace with Gemini for research, summarization, legal review, data filtering across 4.7M connected vehicles | Cross-functional productivity |
    50	| Employee | Routematic | Migrated entire infrastructure to Google Cloud (Compute Engine, GKE) in 8 months with zero downtime | Release cycles shortened from **weeks to days** |
    51	| Employee | 704 Apps | Gemini analyzes in-trip audio to measure emotional "temperature" and flag hostile language for safety alerts | Real-time safety monitoring |
    52	| Code | Renault Group (Ampere) | Enterprise Gemini Code Assist understands company code base, standards, and conventions | Developer productivity for EV software |
    53	
    54	## Headline ROI and Impact Numbers Across Industries
    55	
    56	Several organizations reported quantified business outcomes:
    57	
    58	- **Mercari** (Japan's largest online marketplace): Anticipates **500% ROI** while reducing employee workloads by **20%** through AI-powered customer service.
    59	- **LUXGEN**: Customer service agent workload reduced by **30%** with Vertex AI chatbot.
    60	- **Toyota**: Factory AI platform saved over **10,000 man-hours per year**.
    61	- **PODS / Tombras**: Generated **6,000+ unique ad headlines** across all 299 NYC neighborhoods in just **29 hours**.
    62	- **Virgin Voyages**: Uses Veo text-to-video to create **thousands of hyper-personalized ads and emails** in a single batch without sacrificing brand voice.
    63	- **Figma**: Enables organizations to create high-quality, brand-approved images and assets **in seconds**.
    64	- **Commerzbank**: Making it easier than ever to reach a customer service agent via gen AI.
    65	
    66	## Cross-Industry Patterns
    67	
    68	Three dominant patterns emerge across the 1,001 use cases:
    69	
    70	1. **Conversational Customer Agents** are the most visible entry point — automotive (Mercedes-Benz, GM, VW, LUXGEN), financial services (Commerzbank), and retail (Mercari) all deploy AI-powered virtual assistants to handle customer queries, reduce wait times, and lower human agent workloads.
    71	
    72	2. **Employee Productivity Agents** are the broadest category — companies like Uber, Rivian, Geotab, and Oxa use Gemini for Google Workspace to summarize documents, accelerate research, draft content, review legal documents, and filter data across departments from HR to engineering.
    73	
    74	3. **Creative and Scale Agents** represent the fastest-growing frontier — Virgin Voyages' hyper-personalized video campaigns, PODS' real-time adaptive billboards, and Figma's instant brand-approved asset generation demonstrate that gen AI is moving from text into multimodal creative production at enterprise scale.
    75	
    76	## Key Findings
    77	
    78	- **10× growth in 18 months**: The list expanded from 101 to 1,001 use cases between April 2024 and October 2025, reflecting accelerating enterprise gen AI adoption.
    79	- **Customer and Employee agents dominate**: Conversational assistants and workplace productivity tools are the most common deployment patterns across all 11 industries.
    80	- **Measurable ROI is being achieved in production**: Organizations report outcomes including 500% ROI (Mercari), 30% workload reduction (LUXGEN), 10,000+ man-hours saved annually (Toyota), and thousands of creative assets generated in hours (Virgin Voyages, PODS).
    81	- **Six agent types provide a useful adoption framework**: Customer, Employee, Creative, Code, Data, and Security agents offer enterprises a structured way to identify and prioritize gen AI opportunities.
    82	- **The pace is accelerating**: With 400 new entries added in the latest update alone, the trajectory suggests enterprise gen AI deployment is still in its early exponential phase.

    10	
    11	## When to Use
    12	
    13	Use when the main artifact is a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation or `.pptx` deck, especially when layouts, templates, placeholders, notes, comments, charts, extraction, editing, or final visual quality matter.
    14	
    15	## Core Rules
    16	
    17	### 1. Choose the workflow before touching the deck
    18	
    19	- Reading text, editing an existing deck, rebuilding from a template, and creating from scratch are different jobs with different failure modes.
    20	- For text extraction or inspection, read the deck before editing it.
    21	- Text extraction plus thumbnail-style visual inspection is safer than editing from shape assumptions alone.
    22	- For template-driven work, inventory the deck before replacing content.
    23	- For deep edits, remember a `.pptx` file is OOXML with separate parts for slides, layouts, masters, media, notes, and comments.
    24	- If a template exists, template fidelity beats generic slide-design instincts.
    25	- Reusing or duplicating a good existing slide is often safer than rebuilding it and hoping the theme still matches.
    26	
    27	### 2. Inventory the deck before replacing content
    28	
    29	- Count the reusable layouts, real placeholders, notes, comments, media, and recurring typography or color patterns first.
    30	- Placeholder indexes and layout indexes are not portable assumptions.
    31	- Inspect the actual slide or template before targeting title, body, chart, or image shapes.
    32	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked assets can live outside the visible slide surface.
    33	- A missing or wrong placeholder target can silently land content in the wrong box or wrong layer.
    34	- Master and layout settings can override local slide edits, so the visible problem is not always on the slide you are editing.
    35	
    36	### 3. Match content to the actual placeholders
    37	
    38	- Count the actual content pieces before choosing a layout.
    39	- Pick layouts based on the real number of ideas, columns, images, or charts the slide needs.
    40	- Do not force two ideas into a three-column slide or cram dense text under a chart.
    41	- Category counts and data series lengths must match or charts will break in ugly ways.
    42	- Explicit sizing beats wishful thinking: text boxes, images, and charts need real space, not "it should fit".
    43	- Do not choose a layout with more placeholders than the content can meaningfully fill.
    44	- Quote layouts are for real quotes, and image-led layouts are for slides that actually have images.
    45	- For chart-, table-, or image-heavy slides, full-slide or two-column layouts are usually safer than stacking dense text above the visual.
    46	
    47	### 4. Preserve the deck's visual language
    48	
    49	- Theme, master, and layout files usually decide fonts, colors, and hierarchy more than any one slide does.
    50	- Start from the deck's actual theme, fonts, spacing, and aspect ratio instead of improvising a new style.
    51	- Reuse the deck's own alignment and spacing system instead of inventing a second visual language.
    52	- Use common fonts for portability and strong contrast for readability.
    53	- Preserve the template's visual logic first; originality matters less than not breaking the deck's existing language.
    54	- Combining slides from multiple sources requires normalizing themes, masters, and alignment afterward.
    55	
    56	### 5. Run content QA and visual QA separately
    57	
    58	- Text overflow, bad alignment, clipped shapes, weak contrast, and placeholder leftovers are normal first-pass failures.
    59	- Run both content QA and visual QA; missing text and broken layout are different failure classes.
    60	- Render or inspect the actual deck output before delivery when layout matters.
    61	- Search for leftover template junk, sample labels, and placeholder text before calling the deck finished.
    62	- Check notes, comments, labels, legends, and chart/table semantics separately from the visual pass.
    63	- A deck can pass text extraction and still fail on overlap, clipping, wrong theme inheritance, or broken notes.
    64	- Thumbnail grids and rendered slides usually reveal layout bugs faster than code or text inspection.
    65	- Assume the first render is wrong and do at least one fix-and-verify cycle before calling the deck finished.
    66	- Re-check affected slides after each fix because one spacing change often creates another issue.
    67	
    68	### 6. Keep decks portable and review-safe
    69	
    70	- Template masters can override direct edits in surprising ways.
    71	- Complex effects may degrade across PowerPoint, LibreOffice, and conversion pipelines, so keep important content robust without them.
    72	- Image sizing, font substitution, and placeholder mismatch are common reasons a deck looks good in code and bad on screen.
    73	- Notes, comments, linked media, and merged decks can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    74	
    75	## Common Traps
    76	
    77	- Placeholder text and sample charts often survive template reuse if not explicitly replaced.
    78	- Directly editing one slide can fail if the real issue lives in the master or layout.
    79	- Charts, icons, and text boxes need enough space; near-collisions are usually visible only after rendering.
    80	- Layout indexes vary by template, so built-in assumptions from one deck often break in another.
    81	- A missing placeholder or wrong shape target can silently put content in the wrong place.
    82	- Counting the text ideas after choosing the layout usually leads to empty placeholders, weak hierarchy, or leftover template junk.
    83	- Font substitution can move line breaks and wreck careful spacing.
    84	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked media can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    85	- A deck can pass text inspection and still fail visually because of overlap, contrast, or edge clipping.
    86	- Editing from one slide alone can miss the real source of truth in the theme, master, or layout definitions.
    87	- Choosing a quote, comparison, or multi-column layout without matching content usually makes the deck look templated rather than intentional.
    88	- Combining or duplicating slides without checking masters and themes can create subtle inconsistency slide by slide.
    89	- Aspect-ratio mismatches like `16:9` versus `4:3` can shift every placement decision even when each slide looks locally reasonable.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build a 7-slide, 16:9 PowerPoint presentation from the Google Cloud Gen AI use-case brief.
Follows the task_input.json slide outline and uses only data from source_brief.md.
"""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)

# Google Cloud-inspired palette (data-forward, strategic)
DARK_BLUE = RgbColor(0x1A, 0x23, 0x7E)      # Deep navy primary
MEDIUM_BLUE = RgbColor(0x42, 0x85, 0xF4)    # Google blue accent
LIGHT_BLUE = RgbColor(0xE8, 0xF0, 0xFE)     # Soft blue background
ACCENT_ORANGE = RgbColor(0xEA, 0x43, 0x35)  # Accent for highlights
DARK_GRAY = RgbColor(0x20, 0x20, 0x20)      # Primary text
MEDIUM_GRAY = RgbColor(0x5F, 0x63, 0x68)    # Secondary text
WHITE = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GRAY = RgbColor(0xF5, 0xF5, 0xF5)
GREEN = RgbColor(0x34, 0xA8, 0x53)          # Positive metric

MARGIN_TOP = Inches(0.4)

def set_slide_bg_color(slide, color_hex):
    """Set solid background color for a slide."""
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color_hex


def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=Pt(18),
                font_color=DARK_GRAY, bold=False, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Calibri", valign=MSO_ANCHOR.TOP):
    """Add a formatted text box."""
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    tf.auto_size = None
    tf.anchor = valign
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.color.rgb = font_color
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return txBox


def add_bullet_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets,
                       font_size=Pt(18), font_color=DARK_GRAY,
                       font_name="Calibri", line_spacing=1.2,
                       bullet_color=MEDIUM_BLUE):
    """Add a text box with bullet paragraphs."""
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    tf.auto_size = None
    tf.anchor = MSO_ANCHOR.TOP

    for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = bullet
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = font_color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.level = 0
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
        # bullet via font symbol
        p.text = "•  " + bullet
    return txBox


def add_rounded_rect(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color, line_color=None):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    if line_color:

    else:

    return shape

                number, font_size=Pt(32), font_color=DARK_BLUE, bold=True,
                align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER, valign=MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE)

                label, font_size=Pt(14), font_color=MEDIUM_GRAY,
                align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER, valign=MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE)
    if sublabel:
        add_textbox(slide, left, top + Inches(1.0), width, Inches(0.25),
                    sublabel, font_size=Pt(11), font_color=MEDIUM_GRAY,
                    align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER, valign=MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE)
    return card

def build_patterns_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg_color(slide, WHITE)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT, MARGIN_TOP, SLIDE_WIDTH - Inches(1), Inches(0.7),
                "Common Patterns: Customer Assistants, Employee Productivity, and Creative Scale",
                font_size=Pt(32), font_color=DARK_BLUE, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    col_w = Inches(3.9)
    col_h = Inches(4.2)
    gap = Inches(0.3)
    start_x = (SLIDE_WIDTH - col_w * 3 - gap * 2) / 2
    start_y = Inches(1.5)

    columns = [
        {
            "title": "Conversational Customer Agents",
            "color": MEDIUM_BLUE,
            "items": [
                "Mercedes-Benz — MBUX Virtual Assistant powered by Gemini via Vertex AI enables natural driver conversations for navigation and POI.",
                "General Motors (OnStar) — Virtual assistant with Google Cloud conversational AI recognizes speaker intent.",
                "Volkswagen of America — myVW app virtual assistant lets drivers query owner's manuals; multimodal camera feature for dashboard indicators.",
                "LUXGEN — AI agent on LINE answers customer questions via Vertex AI; reduced human CS workload by 30%.",
                "Commerzbank — Making it easier than ever to reach a customer service agent via gen AI.",
            ],
        },
        {
            "title": "Employee Productivity Agents",
            "color": GREEN,
            "items": [
                "Uber — AI agents summarize CS communications and surface prior interaction context.",
                "Rivian — Gemini in Google Workspace for instant research, accelerated learning, and rapid skill acquisition.",
                "Rivian — NotebookLM centralizes FAQ answers with verified sources and interactive chat.",
                "Geotab — Google Workspace with Gemini for research, summarization, legal review, data filtering across 4.7M connected vehicles.",
                "Routematic — Migrated entire infrastructure to Google Cloud in 8 months with zero downtime; release cycles shortened from weeks to days.",

        },
        {
            "title": "Creative and Scale Agents",
            "color": ACCENT_ORANGE,
            "items": [
                "Virgin Voyages — Uses Veo text-to-video to create thousands of hyper-personalized ads and emails in a single batch without sacrificing brand voice.",
                "PODS / Tombras — 'World's Smartest Billboard' on trucks adapted to NYC neighborhoods in real time using Gemini.",
                "Figma — Enables organizations to create high-quality, brand-approved images and assets in seconds.",
            ],
        },
    ]

    for idx, col in enumerate(columns):
        x = start_x + idx * (col_w + gap)
        # Header bar
        hdr = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, x, start_y, col_w, Inches(0.45))
        hdr.fill.solid()
        hdr.fill.fore_color.rgb = col["color"]
        hdr.line.fill.background()
        add_textbox(slide, x, start_y, col_w, Inches(0.45),
                    col["title"], font_size=Pt(15), font_color=WHITE, bold=True,
                    align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER, valign=MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE)

        # Body box
        body = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, x, start_y + Inches(0.45), col_w, col_h)
        body.fill.solid()
        body.fill.fore_color.rgb = LIGHT_GRAY
        body.line.fill.background()

        tf = body.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        tf.auto_size = None
        tf.margin_left = Inches(0.12)
        tf.margin_right = Inches(0.12)
        tf.margin_top = Inches(0.12)
        tf.margin_bottom = Inches(0.12)
        tf.anchor = MSO_ANCHOR.TOP

        for i, item in enumerate(col["items"]):
            if i == 0:
                p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            else:
                p = tf.add_paragraph()
            p.text = "• " + item
            p.font.size = Pt(12)
            p.font.color.rgb = DARK_GRAY
            p.font.name = "Calibri"
            p.space_after = Pt(8)

    # Annotation
    add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT, Inches(6.2), SLIDE_WIDTH - Inches(1), Inches(0.5),
                "Three dominant patterns emerge across the 1,001 use cases. Customer and Employee agents dominate today; Creative agents represent the fastest-growing frontier as gen AI moves from text into multimodal production.",

    return slide


def build_takeaways_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg_color(slide, DARK_BLUE)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT, MARGIN_TOP, SLIDE_WIDTH - Inches(1), Inches(0.7),
                "Takeaways: Where to Start and What to Expect from Enterprise Gen AI",
                font_size=Pt(34), font_color=WHITE, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    takeaways = [
        ("1. Gen AI is production-ready across all major industries",
         "1,001 real-world deployments across 11 verticals prove the technology has moved beyond pilot phase."),
        ("2. Customer and Employee agents are the most common entry points",
         "Conversational assistants and workplace productivity tools offer the clearest, fastest paths to measurable ROI."),
        ("3. Measurable ROI is achievable within months",
         "Organizations report 500% ROI (Mercari), 30% workload reduction (LUXGEN), and 10,000+ hours saved annually (Toyota)."),
        ("4. Creative and Code agents are emerging fast",
         "Virgin Voyages, PODS, and Figma demonstrate multimodal creative production at enterprise scale; Renault Ampere shows code-agent maturity."),
        ("5. The pace of adoption is accelerating — early movers gain compounding advantages",
         "10× growth in 18 months with 400 new entries in the latest update alone suggests enterprise gen AI is still in its early exponential phase."),
    ]

    y = Inches(1.4)
    for title, body in takeaways:
        # Number circle
        circle = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, MARGIN_LEFT, y + Inches(0.05), Inches(0.35), Inches(0.35))
        circle.fill.solid()
        circle.fill.fore_color.rgb = MEDIUM_BLUE
        circle.line.fill.background()

        add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT, y + Inches(0.05), Inches(0.35), Inches(0.35),
                    title.split(".")[0], font_size=Pt(16), font_color=WHITE, bold=True,
                    align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER, valign=MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE)

        # Title text
        add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT + Inches(0.5), y, SLIDE_WIDTH - Inches(1.2), Inches(0.35),
                    title, font_size=Pt(18), font_color=WHITE, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, valign=MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE)

        # Body text
        add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT + Inches(0.5), y + Inches(0.35), SLIDE_WIDTH - Inches(1.2), Inches(0.45),
                    body, font_size=Pt(14), font_color=LIGHT_BLUE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, valign=MSO_ANCHOR.TOP)

        y += Inches(1.05)

    # Footer
    add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT, Inches(6.7), SLIDE_WIDTH - Inches(1), Inches(0.3),
                "Source: Google Cloud Blog — '1,001 real-world gen AI use cases from the world's leading organizations' (October 2025)",
                font_size=Pt(11), font_color=MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    return slide


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main():
    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = SLIDE_WIDTH
    prs.slide_height = SLIDE_HEIGHT

    build_title_slide(prs)
    build_growth_slide(prs)
    build_taxonomy_slide(prs)
    build_automotive_slide(prs)
    build_roi_slide(prs)
    build_patterns_slide(prs)
    build_takeaways_slide(prs)

    output_path = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"
    prs.save(output_path)
    print(f"Saved: {output_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
